reliability_summary: Chevrolet Spark overall reliability is decent (JD Power ~82/100; owners commonly reach 100k+ miles with maintenance), but earlier US-spec Sparks (2014-2017) with the 4-speed automatic have a well-documented pattern of transmission slipping/hesitation around 60,000-80,000 miles, repairs averaging ~$2,680, per CarComplaints/TrueDelta/RepairPal. This 2019 unit, however, is the post-Jan-2019 facelift sold with a CVT automatic only (per Israeli sources), a different unit than the flagged 4-speed, so the known transmission-failure pattern doesn't directly transfer, but there's little independent long-term data yet on this specific CVT. Israeli forum sentiment is mixed-to-positive short/mid-term (quiet, low running cost, decent build for the segment) with some concern about durability past ~5 years typical of budget Korean-built GM models. No major engine-specific complaints surfaced. Confidence is medium: reliability data is asymmetric across model years/markets and the specific 2019 CVT combo is thinly documented.

reliability_summary: This 2012-2015 i20 uses the 1.4 Gamma MPI engine with a simple 4-speed torque-converter automatic (A4CF1), not the troubled 7-speed DCT found on later/other Hyundai-Kia models, so overall verdict is above-average reliability for the segment. The A4CF1 gearbox has documented weak points (jerky shifts, solenoid wear, clutch-pack friction wear) typically surfacing around 60-80k km, especially under stop-and-go city use, but responds well to fluid changes every 40-50k km. The 1.4 Gamma engine can show oil consumption and timing-chain-tensioner rattle at higher mileage, though carbon buildup issues cited in some sources apply mainly to GDI variants, likely not this MPI unit. At 144k km this car is well past where transmission/engine wear symptoms typically start, so a pre-purchase transmission fluid/behavior check and oil-consumption check are warranted. Israeli owner sentiment (auto.co.il/carzone) leans positive ('reliable, no major issues') for this generation. Confidence is medium: no major recalls or NHTSA/CarComplaints-scale data found specific to this exact combo, and Israeli-specific threads were general rather than deep-dive.

reliability_summary: The 2014-2019 i10 generation scores well on independent surveys (What Car? 98.6%, 4th of 19 in class; Auto Express Driver Power top-3), with no notable systemic faults for the 1.2L Kappa engine used here (the 1.0L variant has separate timing-chain wear reports around 100,000km that don't apply to this 87hp 1.2L). The 4-speed automatic gets scattered owner-forum complaints - delayed engagement from park/reverse, occasional jerky or slipping shifts - but these read as intermittent/maintenance-related (fluid, TCM, TSB reflash) rather than a known design flaw. Common minor issues across the model: above-average brake pad wear, dashboard rattles in cold weather, and occasional electrical gremlins - all low-cost. Israeli forum threads flag gearbox complaints (jerky shifts, unexpected engagement) similar to the English-language reports. Confidence is medium: survey data is strong and consistent, but automatic-specific and Israeli-market data is thinner and more anecdotal. Sources: What Car?, Auto Express, TrueDelta, Hyundai Forums/Team-BHP, carsforum.co.il/icar.co.il.

reliability_summary: Chevrolet Spark 2016 with the 1.4L/98hp engine and CVT automatic sits below average overall (CarComplaints ranks Spark ~26th of 40 Chevy models; top complaint categories are powertrain, engine oil consumption, and electrical), though 2016 is regarded as a better year than the trouble-plagued 2013-2014 models. The key concern is that an Israeli source states the CVT gearbox defect causing rough/unsafe shifting was only fixed in mid-2017 production, meaning this 2016-built car predates that fix. US owner data is mixed: some CVTs failed around 50k-80k miles requiring ~$2,680 replacement, while other owners report 200k+ miles trouble-free, and transmission complaints are less frequent than electrical/oil-consumption issues in aggregate. This listing's 51,700 km (~32k mi) is below where most reported transmission failures occur, so current risk is limited but not eliminated. Given the known pre-mid-2017 CVT flaw, score is capped at 5 per reliability rubric; confidence is medium due to conflicting evidence and no Spark-specific Israeli recall data found. Sources: CarComplaints.com, TrueDelta, KBB consumer reviews, cmotors.co.il, JustAnswer forum threads.
